focus: The cross-package ledger: the coverage-graph duplication treaty (two skills, one parity test, shared/ hosts neither), the 19-claim death-row certification at full sweep, the cli->@spec-kit/shared census (18 lanes) against the 2023-era shim registry, and the js-yaml single-importer verdict.
noveltyJustification: All 4 new; the treaty is the strongest exhibit (cross-skill RELATIVE import as the unification mechanism, production copy in the OTHER skill, shared/ hosting neither), the certification overturned no prior claim while sharpening 19 counts, the shim census killed lib/trigger-extractor.js and corrected f-iter004-004 (embeddings arrives, as two constants), and js-yaml survives on one helper.
keyQuestions: Does the package framing (context generation and continuity management) match what the code does, and which helpers are duplicated across this package, ../lib/, and any shared layer?
Which directories or entry points have zero external callers, and which registry entries point at nothing?
ruledOut: cli/lib/coverage-graph/ is the production copy: its own package production importers NONE-FOUND; the deep-loop copy has production neighbors
js-yaml backs the frontmatter parsing: that is shared/frontmatter/parse-frontmatter (11 lanes); js-yaml survives on one helper

label: The coverage-graph engine is duplicated across two skills and unified by a TEST, not a module: cli/lib/coverage-graph/*.ts (spec-kit copy, ZERO production importers in its own package; 13 test suites: 8+ here, 5 across the fence) vs system-deep-loop/runtime/lib/coverage-graph/{signals,query}.ts (the PRODUCTION copy with its own types and database); the treaty = tests/graph-convergence-parity.vitest.ts:6-11, a cross-skill SIBLING-RELATIVE import (../../../system-deep-loop/...) pinning both signals implementations; shared/ — the sanctioned seam — hosts neither; plus the stray cli/lib/coverage-graph-convergence.cjs. Recommendation: merge — one copy in @spec-kit/shared or the deep-loop; retire the treaty.

Certification rollup (closes Q4): all 19 no-caller claims re-verified at FULL sweep (tests+docs+fixtures included, self-mentions counted); no claim overturned; counts: continuity/ast-parser 0, setup/_utils 0, .scan-one 0, quality-kpi 1 (self), cli/doctor 1 (self), migrate-deep-research-paths 1 (changelog), the 3 evals harnesses 2 (one = evals/README), registry-loader 2, check-smart-router 2, spec/sweep-track-roots 2, fix-memory-h1 3, rank-memories 5 (all docs), the retrieval quartet 4-8 (docs+fixtures). Removal bill: ~30 files + 2 directories, each evidence-filed (f-iter002-003, f-iter003-002/003, f-iter006-001/002/003, f-iter008-002/003). Recommendation: remove in one PR with the docs lines they ship.

The sanctioned seam works; its 2023-era shadow does not: the cli->@spec-kit/shared census = 18 lanes/43+ citations (frontmatter/parse-frontmatter 11, memory-sufficiency 5, path-security 4, trigger-extractor 4) versus the registry libraries[]javascript (8 re-export shims): lib/trigger-extractor.js = ZERO importers (dead-but-registered), lib/embeddings.js = ONE caller for TWO CONSTANTS (core/workflow.ts:56, correcting f-iter004-004), the other six = 1-6 citations (alive); plus the stray coverage-graph-convergence.cjs. Recommendation: fix — re-derive libraries[] from this census, or execute the f-iter002-001 registry-removal.

js-yaml: a top-level dependency with ONE production importer (rules/check-grep-convention-helper.mjs) + 2 tests + an ambient .d.ts, while 11 importers take their YAML via shared/frontmatter/parse-frontmatter. Recommendation: merge — put the one helper YAML need behind the shared seam (or downgrade the dep into that helper).
